title: Click a dark blue rack location in RMS/map view to reveal the tote number shown on that rack
summary: In the OptiSweep RMS/map view, use the rack color and click interaction to reveal which tote the system associates with a specific rack location. Compare the displayed tote number to the expected tote number reported by a caller to confirm whether the rack has the correct tote.
when_to_use: Use when a caller reports an expected tote number for a rack location, but you need to verify which tote the system currently shows on that rack (especially when the rack appears dark blue/violet indicating a tote is present).
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the RMS/map view rack verification by selecting the correct object type (container selection) and clicking the dark blue rack to read the tote number shown for that rack.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to click the rack/container on the RMS/map view

system_preconditions: The target rack location must be visible in the RMS/map view and appear dark blue/violet (tote present) for the click-to-reveal tote number behavior described in the source.

visual_references.description: RMS/map view rack locations: dark blue/violet indicates a tote is on the rack; click the rack to reveal the tote number on the rack.
RMS/map view container selection behavior: selecting container selection shows a box icon and the tote number; includes color meaning (dark blue tote present, light blue empty).

steps.title: Find the rack location you need to verify in the RMS/map view
steps.purpose: Identify the exact rack location to verify against the expected tote number.
steps.instruction: In the RMS/map view, locate the rack location that you need to verify.
steps.expected_result: You have a specific rack location selected/identified on the RMS/map view that you can click after choosing the correct object selection mode.
steps.healthy_condition: The rack location you intend to verify is visible and appears as a rack/container object in the map view.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reliably identify the intended rack location on the map (wrong rack clicked or ambiguous location).

actions.label: Locate rack on RMS/map view
actions.exact_action: Find the rack location you need to verify.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “What are these These are rack locations, right …”

steps.title: Confirm the rack is dark blue/violet (tote present) using the rack color meaning
steps.purpose: Ensure the rack has a tote present so the click-to-reveal tote number behavior applies.
steps.instruction: Check the rack color on the RMS/map view: confirm it is dark blue/violet (tote present) rather than light blue (empty).
steps.expected_result: The rack you will click is dark blue/violet, indicating a tote is on the rack.
steps.healthy_condition: Dark blue/violet rack tone corresponds to “has a tote on it”; light blue corresponds to “empty rack.”
steps.failure_condition: The rack appears light blue (empty), meaning it may not have the tote you expect.

actions.label: Verify rack color
actions.exact_action: Confirm the rack is dark blue (tote present) using the documented rack color meaning.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “There are two distinct color on this … dark blue almost like a Violet … If a rack has this dark blue tone, it means it has a toad on it. If … light blue … it means it’s empty.”

steps.title: Select container selection, then click the rack/container itself to reveal rack details
steps.purpose: Trigger the RMS/map view interaction that displays the tote number associated with the clicked rack.
steps.instruction: In RMS/map view, use the container selection object mode, then physically click the rack/container itself to reveal more information about that rack.
steps.expected_result: After clicking the dark blue rack (with container selection selected), the UI reveals the tote number associated with that rack.
steps.healthy_condition: The click interaction is performed on the rack/container itself (not just on the map background), with container selection selected so the rack click returns rack/tote details.
steps.failure_condition: No tote number appears after clicking (often due to not using container selection or clicking the wrong object type).

actions.label: Click the rack/container
actions.exact_action: physically click on the container itself

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “So to look at more information about the rack, you have to click on the container selection and then physically click on the container itself to learn more about this.”
“When a rack is dark blue, if you click on it, it will tell you what tote you have on the rack itself.”

steps.title: Read the tote number displayed for that rack
steps.purpose: Capture the system-reported tote number associated with the clicked rack for comparison.
steps.instruction: After clicking the dark blue rack, read the tote number displayed for that rack.
steps.expected_result: A tote number is displayed for the clicked rack (the tote associated with that rack).
steps.healthy_condition: The tote number shown corresponds to the tote on the rack (dark blue/violet rack tone).
steps.failure_condition: No tote number is displayed, or the displayed value is unclear/unreadable.

actions.label: Read tote number
actions.exact_action: Read the tote number displayed for that rack after clicking.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “When a rack is dark blue, if you click on it, it will tell you what tote you have on the rack itself.”

steps.title: Compare the displayed tote number to the expected tote number from the caller
steps.purpose: Determine whether the rack contains the expected tote or whether there is a mismatch requiring further recovery investigation.
steps.instruction: Compare the tote number displayed for the rack to the expected tote number reported by the caller.
steps.expected_result: You determine whether the displayed tote number matches the expected tote number (example in source: caller expects HV 110 but click shows 113).
steps.healthy_condition: Displayed tote number equals the expected tote number.
steps.failure_condition: Displayed tote number does not match the expected tote number (example: expected HV 110, displayed 113).

actions.label: Compare tote numbers
actions.exact_action: Compare the displayed tote number to the expected tote number

stop_or_escalate_if: If the displayed tote number does not match the expected tote number, stop and escalate for further recovery investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “So if someone’s telling you like I see HV 110 on this rack and then you click on the rack and you see 113 … you see … there’s something wrong with it. It’s not the right tote.”

success_criteria: The tote number associated with the clicked dark blue/violet rack is displayed in RMS/map view.
The displayed tote number can be directly compared to the expected tote number reported by the caller.
healthy_conditions: Dark blue/violet rack tone indicates a tote is present on the rack.
Clicking the rack after selecting container selection reveals the tote number for that rack.
failure_conditions: Rack appears light blue (empty) when you expect a tote.
After selecting container selection and clicking the rack, no tote number is displayed.
Displayed tote number does not match the expected tote number (indicating the wrong tote may be on the rack).
escalation_guidance: If the displayed tote number does not match the expected tote number, stop and escalate for further recovery investigation (the source indicates this can mean the wrong tote is on the rack).
